title: Measuring responses of budding yeast strains to extracellular changes using microfluidics
author: Clark, Crane, et al.
materials: Yeast nitrogen base without amino acids

steps.title: Make filtered SC media with BSA
steps.instruction: Prepare synthetic complete (SC) medium containing 2 % (w/v) glucose and add BSA (concentration not specified); filter the medium through a 0.2 µm filter to ensure sterility and remove particles that could block the microfluidic device.

steps.title: Inoculate strains into media
steps.instruction: From each of the five pre‑prepared plates, pick a single colony of the corresponding Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain and inoculate it into 5 mL of the filtered SC + 2 % glucose medium.

steps.title: Overnight incubation of cultures
steps.instruction: Incubate the inoculated cultures at 30 °C with shaking for approximately 6 hours (overnight) to allow growth into logarithmic phase.

steps.title: Dilute cultures to OD 0.1
steps.instruction: Measure the optical density (OD) of each overnight culture using a GE Ultrospec 10; then dilute each culture into 5 mL of fresh filtered SC + 2 % glucose medium so that the final OD is 0.1, ensuring low cell density and minimal competition for resources.

steps.title: Final incubation before experiment
steps.instruction: Incubate the diluted cultures at 30 °C with shaking for 3–4 hours before loading them into the microfluidic device.

description: The following protocol describes the steps needed to observe the nuclear translocation of five Saccharomyces transcription factors in response to a rapid drop in the extracellular glucose concentration.1 However, the ability to culture 5 strains in parallel, to vary the environment and to observe individual cells over many hours provides many additional applications. We have also used the protocol to investigate the timing of changes in ribosome biogenesis,2 to demonstrate real-time control of media conditions in response to changes in cell growth rate2 and to study signaling pathways3,4 and metabolic oscillations5 in S. cerevisiae, as well as to characterize cell cycle arrest and kinetochore protein localization in the human pathogen Cryptococcus neoformans.6,7,8 Variations on the protocol could include different modes of measurement, such as fluorescence intensity rather than localization, ratiometric measures and fluorescence lifetimes. Constant, or gradually changing media conditions could also be imposed rather than a step change.
